rubric_hint.rule: 1 eligible species recorded beyond 250 m but within 1000 m, none within 250 m
rubric_hint.basis: prompts/rubric.md v1 applied to all rings 0-1000 m and effort; a default, not a verdict

reasons.claim: 5.09 ha regeneration felling notification, status notified. Completed felling overlaps the polygon by 0.001 ha (about 0%), so it is not ALREADY_FELLED.
No eligible species lies within 250 m. The only threatened species in the 250 m ring is the mobile bird Sturnus vulgaris (VU), plus NT birds, which are supporting evidence only.

One eligible species lies beyond 250 m but within 1000 m: Sarcosoma globosum (EN, site-bound fungus, forest-associated, threatened by lack of continuity forest, lack of old/large trees and forestry ground disturbance). Its nearest record is 489 m away (uncertainty 25 m, 2016), and it has 3 records with the latest in 2017. This meets the rubric's MEDIUM rule.
Effort is adequate: 1077 records within 1000 m against a county median of 724 (83rd percentile). 60 records from 35 species lie within 250 m, and none lie inside the polygon.

uncertainties: The only eligible record is old (2016-2017) and 489 m away, so it may not reflect the present state of the stand. The rubric hint still gives MEDIUM, and I did not override it.
58 records within 250 m were dropped for coordinate uncertainty above the ring allowance, so close-by coarse records are not counted.
Two NT forest fungi (Hydnellum peckii, Porodaedalea pini) lie at 592-600 m. They have no bearing on the rubric beyond 250 m.
not_established: That Sarcosoma globosum or any other threatened species occupies the polygon or its surroundings now.
That felling would harm any recorded species.
Absence of eligible records inside or within 250 m does not show their absence; the polygon has 0 records.
next_action: Have a reviewer check the 2016 Sarcosoma globosum records, about 490 m away, against the stand's habitat and decide whether a field check is warranted before felling starts.
